interest: Shows SCAP–Washington debate over reopening Japan's international telecommunications in 1946, including Korea's priority and foreign exchange worries.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP)
overview: This file contains War Department and Department of State correspondence, draft cables, and incoming and outgoing telegrams from August to October 1946 concerning the re-establishment and regulation of international telecommunications to and from occupied Japan. Despite the State Department decimal filing title referring to the protection of Ecuadorian interests (311.22), the documents focus entirely on policy negotiations between General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (GHQ SCAP), the War Department's Civil Affairs Division (CAD), and the State Department's Division of Communication and Records (A-H). Key matters addressed include SCAP's proposals to reopen telegraphic and first-class postal communications for personal and commercial messages under strict military censorship, the financial and foreign exchange mechanics of telegraph receipts (prepaid yen versus dollar accounts for essential imports), the diplomatic requirement of extending services to liberated Korea before or simultaneously with Japan, and the establishment of relay communication circuits connecting Japan via San Francisco with U.S. military bases and territories across the Pacific (including Tahiti, New Caledonia, Fiji, Samoa, Guam, Midway, Alaska, and the Panama Canal Zone).

subfiles.about: War Department outgoing cable conveying Washington agency comments and policy reservations on SCAP's plan to reopen international telecommunications with Japan.
subfiles.summary: War Department replies to SCAP on reopening Japan's telecommunications: Korea first, concern over yen-prepaid messages draining foreign exchange, and telephone traffic restricted.
subfiles.title: Outgoing War Department Telegram WAR 80409 to CINCAFPAC on Reestablishment of Telecommunications with Japan
subfiles.to: Commander-in-Chief, Army Forces in the Pacific (CINCAFPAC, Tokyo)

subfiles.about: State Department transmittal memorandum submitting a draft cable to CINCAFPAC regarding the reopening of telecommunications with Japan for War Department review.
subfiles.from: B. O'Sullivan (Department of State, Division of Communication and Records, A-H)
subfiles.summary: B. O'Sullivan forwards a draft cable to CINCAFPAC on reopening telecommunications with Japan for War Department concurrence; it was dispatched October 4.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from B. O'Sullivan to Colonel Socks Transmitting Draft Cable on Telecommunications with Japan
subfiles.to: Colonel Socks (Executive Officer, Civil Affairs Division, War Department)

subfiles.about: State Department draft cable to SCAP outlining policy conditions for resuming international telecommunications, including a revised insert on carrier revenues and foreign exchange.
subfiles.from: W. E. O'Connor (Department of State, Telecommunications Division / A-H)
subfiles.summary: Draft cable to SCAP, with W. E. O'Connor's revised paragraph of October 1, 1946, questioning whether yen payments would reduce foreign exchange for essential imports.
subfiles.title: Draft Cable from War Department to SCAP with Revised Paragraph on Foreign Exchange and Telecommunications Financing
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP, Tokyo)

subfiles.about: State Department draft cable setting forth detailed comments, accounting queries, and censorship requirements regarding SCAP's international telecommunications plan.
subfiles.from: B. O'Sullivan (Department of State, Division of Communication and Records, A-H)
subfiles.summary: B. O'Sullivan's draft cable to CINCAFPAC: Korea before Japan, doubts on SCAP's terminal accounts, foreign exchange concerns, and non-official traffic limited to telegraphy.
subfiles.title: Draft Cable to CINCAFPAC on Policy for Reopening Telecommunications with Japan
subfiles.to: Commander-in-Chief, Army Forces in the Pacific (CINCAFPAC, Tokyo)

subfiles.about: War Department draft cable replying to SCAP's telecommunications proposals, accompanied by notes on informal clearance by the Treasury Department.
subfiles.summary: September 19, 1946 draft cable giving Korea priority, questioning yen-prepaid telegrams, and accepting SCAP's government, diplomatic, Red Cross and press traffic categories.
subfiles.title: Draft Cable from War Department to SCAP on Reopening Telecommunications with Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP, Tokyo)

subfiles.about: SCAP incoming telegram requesting tariff rates and operational verification for telecommunication services to South Pacific bases and U.S. island territories.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (GHQ SCAP, Tokyo)
subfiles.summary: GHQ SCAP asks the War Department for rates and availability of message services to Papeete, New Caledonia, Suva, Samoa, Alaska, Guam, Midway and other U.S. possessions and bases.
subfiles.title: Incoming Telegram C 65059 from GHQ SCAP Requesting Verification of Telecommunications to Pacific Bases and US Possessions

subfiles.about: War Department outgoing cable authorizing telecommunications between Japan and U.S. military bases in the South Pacific via San Francisco.
subfiles.from: War Department (Civil Affairs Division, Lt. Col. Dice)
subfiles.summary: War Department telegram WAR 99040 authorizes telecommunications from Japan via San Francisco to bases at Papeete, New Caledonia, Suva and Samoa, with word rates, for military and authorized personnel only.
subfiles.title: Outgoing War Department Telegram WAR 99040 to CINCAFPAC Authorizing Telecommunications to South Pacific Bases
subfiles.to: Commander-in-Chief, Army Forces in the Pacific (CINCAFPAC, Tokyo)

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum confirming interagency approval of the proposed cable regarding telecommunications with South Pacific military bases.
subfiles.from: P. P. Claxton (Department of State, Division of Communication and Records, A-H)
subfiles.summary: P. P. Claxton confirms State Department approval of the draft cable to SCAP on South Pacific telecommunications; the War Department dispatched it August 28 as CM-OUT 99040.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from P. P. Claxton to Colonel Chard Confirming State Department Approval of Pacific Cable
subfiles.to: Colonel Chard (Civil Affairs Division, War Department)

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum transmitting a draft cable to CINCAFPAC concerning telecommunications between Japan and South Pacific bases for War Department concurrence.
subfiles.from: B. O'Sullivan (Department of State, SWNCC Directorate)
subfiles.summary: B. O'Sullivan sends the War Department a draft cable on Japan–South Pacific telecommunications, replying to SCAP cable Z-02642; assigned to Lieutenant Colonel Dice.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from B. O'Sullivan to Executive Officer, CAD, Transmitting Draft Cable on South Pacific Telecommunications
subfiles.to: Executive Officer, Civil Affairs Division (CAD), War Department

subfiles.about: State Department draft cable establishing telecommunication services and tariff schedules between Japan and U.S. military bases in the South Pacific.
subfiles.from: B. O'Sullivan (Department of State, Division of Communication and Records, A-H)
subfiles.summary: Draft cable approving telecommunications via San Francisco between Japan and bases at Papeete, New Caledonia, Suva and Samoa, with per-word rates, for military and authorized personnel.
subfiles.title: Draft Cable to CINCAFPAC on Telecommunications Between Japan and South Pacific Bases
subfiles.to: Commander-in-Chief, Army Forces in the Pacific (CINCAFPAC, Tokyo)

subfiles.about: Earlier draft cable outlining proposed telecommunication arrangements between Japan and South Pacific military installations via San Francisco.
subfiles.from: B. O'Sullivan (Department of State, Division of Communication and Records, A-H)
subfiles.summary: B. O'Sullivan's August 20, 1946 draft cable setting tariffs for telecommunications via San Francisco between Japan and bases in Tahiti, New Caledonia, Fiji and Samoa.
subfiles.title: Draft Cable to CINCAFPAC on Telecommunications Between Japan and South Pacific Bases
subfiles.to: Commander-in-Chief, Army Forces in the Pacific (CINCAFPAC, Tokyo)

subfiles.about: SCAP incoming telegram submitting comprehensive policy recommendations for reopening international civil telecommunications to and from Japan.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (GHQ SCAP, Tokyo)
